findings.explanation: `zip` checks only the overlapping prefix and silently ignores a response with fewer or more permission flags than requested IDs. If the backend returns fewer flags and all returned flags are true (including no flags), this condition is false and the function returns all requested IDs for deletion at line 11. Require exact count equality and a true flag for every requested ID; preserve the valid empty/empty case.

`zip` stops at the shorter slice, so if the server returns fewer permission flags than requested IDs and all returned flags are `true`, this condition passes. The function then returns every requested ID on line 11, allowing deletion without a corresponding authorization flag. Reject count mismatches before returning a deletion plan.

`zip` stops at the shorter slice, so a partial permission response with fewer flags than requested IDs is not rejected when all returned flags are `true`. The function then returns every requested ID on line 12, including IDs with no corresponding authorization flag. Require the counts to match before allowing deletion; an empty request with an empty response will still pass that check.

`zip` stops at the shorter collection, so this checks only the permission flags that were returned. If the backend returns fewer flags than requested and all returned flags are true (including an empty response), the check passes and line 11 returns every requested ID for deletion. Require the permission count to match the requested ID count before allowing deletion; the stated contract requires count mismatches to fail closed.

`zip` stops at the shorter input, so this checks only overlapping flags and never verifies that the permission count equals the requested ID count. If the backend returns fewer flags (including an empty response for a nonempty request), the predicate can be false and line 11 returns every requested ID for deletion without a corresponding authorization. Extra flags are likewise ignored. Reject any count mismatch before allowing deletion.

`zip` stops at the shorter input, so this check rejects paired false flags but never detects a permission response with fewer flags than requested IDs. With a nonempty request and an empty or partial `granted` vector containing only true flags, `any` can be false and the function returns `Some` containing every requested ID at line 11. This fails open despite the caller contract requiring a corresponding true flag for every ID; reject count mismatches before returning the IDs.

Reject any count mismatch before evaluating flags. This also preserves the valid empty-request case when both counts are zero.

It also accepts other count mismatches (including an empty request with a nonempty permission response), contrary to the fail-closed contract.
